It is an ambiguity record attached to the `debt` metric, flagged MULTIPLE_SOURCE_CONCEPTS with resolution NO_WINNER_SELECTED. The reason is MULTIPLE_SOURCE_CONCEPTS: the same metric label is attached to two different us-gaap source concepts, and the evidence explicitly states these are different measures rather than two readings of one measure, so the evidence does not establish that either is the figure a question about this metric was asking for. The competing values, for the most recent period (instant 2026-06-27, 10-Q accession 0000320193-26-000020), are: us-gaap:LongTermDebtCurrent = 11,007,000,000 USD and us-gaap:LongTermDebtNoncurrent = 71,340,000,000 USD. The same ambiguity recurs at the two preceding periods: at 2026-03-28, 8,310,000,000 vs 74,404,000,000; at 2025-12-27, 11,827,000,000 vs 76,685,000,000. Both observations at each period carry evidence_state SOURCE_REPORTED and validation_status UNVERIFIABLE, with an empty cross-check list — a single official source cannot cross-validate itself. Each concept is mapped PARTIAL to `debt`, with the registry noting each is a component of total debt, never the total on its own; the concepts also map EXACT to separate metrics (long_term_debt_current, long_term_debt_noncurrent), which is what leaves the registry unable to choose. On which value is correct: the evidence settles nothing. ST-EVA has not selected one and does not claim either is a candidate, and same_measure_established is false. I cannot name a winner. failures.answer: PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets (us-gaap) expresses the capex metric only PARTIALLY, and its figures cannot be read as one continuous comparable series with the metric's other concept. The mapping is recorded on every observation as mapping_type PARTIAL with series_continues = false, and the registry note states the concept 'includes software and other intangible assets, which the property-and-equipment concept does not, so the series does not continue across the change' (e.g. obsarch_5e8e3b741876732ecddb59b4, obsarch_a8700ad3d1771f49f49b06d8). Each observation carries a CONCEPT_MAPPING_BREAK over the window 2007-09-29 to 2014-09-27, so a break is registered at this concept's boundary rather than the series running on. AAPL's issuer adoption confirms the split: PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets is used 2007-09-29 to 2014-09-27 (59 facts, 25 filings), while the other concept, PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment, is mapped EXACT with series_continues = true and is used from 2013-09-28 through 2026-06-27 (105 facts, 47 filings). The two overlap only from 2013-09-28 to 2014-09-27; before that window only the PARTIAL concept was filed, and after it only the EXACT one. In that overlap the two concepts carry identical values for the same periods (8,165,000,000 for 2012-09-30 to 2013-09-28 in obsarch_289495dbc4d35addfdcdef6f and obsarch_cf4f1346ee46ad8e8ddfbd28; 9,571,000,000 for 2013-09-29 to 2014-09-27 in obsarch_a8700ad3d1771f49f49b06d8 and obsarch_8fab7a491f4ecb2c90f1bcf3), but the registry still marks the series as not continuing across the change, so the equivalence at those points does not by itself make the wider run comparable. All figures involved are SOURCE_REPORTED and UNVERIFIABLE (single official source, no cross-check). The capex series itself is complete as held: 164 points, 164 returned, not truncated. The metric is defined as the cash outflow to acquire long-lived assets used in the normal conduct of business, with the definition itself recording that sources differ on whether software and intangibles are included.
